r0030: 14.  On 3 August 1989 the applicant served notice on the tenant requiring her to vacate the apartment.
r0031: 15.  On 14 September 1989 he served notice on her informing her that the order for possession would be enforced by a bailiff on 11 October 1989.
r0032: 16.  On that date, and again on 7 May 1991, the bailiff was unable to evict the tenant, as police assistance was not granted.
r0033: 17.  On 14 December 1991 the applicant applied to the Pescara magistrate (*juge d’instance*) under section 2 of Legislative Decree (*décret-loi*) no. 551/88, converted into Law no. 61/89, for a finding that the tenant had failed to pay the rent and her share of the service charges for the building, and for a declaration that the suspension of the enforcement of evictions did not apply in the present case. On 20 December 1991 the tenant joined the proceedings and contested the applicant’s allegations. A hearing was held before the Pescara magistrate on 2 March 1993. In a decision of 17 April 1993, the magistrate allowed the applicant’s application and declared that the suspension of enforcement did not apply to his case.
r0034: 18.  In the meantime, between 11 May 1991 and 21 April 1993, the bailiff had made nineteen attempts to recover possession. Each attempt proved unsuccessful, as the applicant was not granted police assistance in enforcing the eviction, despite the requests he had made to the Prefect on 12 October and 12 December 1992.
r0035: 19.  On 2 July 1993, when the bailiff went to the premises with police assistance, the tenant vacated the apartment.
r0036: 20.  In the meantime, on 6 November 1992, the Pescara magistrate (*juge d’instance*) had granted an application by the managing agent of the building in which the applicant’s apartment was located for an order requiring the applicant to pay his share of the service charges, together with the share owed by the tenant (a total of ITL 1,406,500, approximately FRF 4,600).
r0038: 21.  Legislative Decree (*décret-loi*) no. 551 of 30 December 1988, converted into Law no. 61 of 21 February 1989 (“Law no. 61/89”), suspended the enforcement of evictions until 30 April 1989. Section 2 of that decree provided that enforcement was not suspended where, in particular, the tenant was in arrears with the rent or the service charges for an amount corresponding to at least two months’ rent.
r0039: 22.  The remainder of the relevant domestic law is described in Immobiliare Saffi v. Italy [GC], no. 22774/93, §§ 18-35, ECHR 1999-V.
